# dsh-modes · Mode Manager
English | 中文
Mode manager for DeepSeek Harness (dsh). It adds a **Modes** page to the Web interface's Settings, w
here you switch what each agent mode can do, edit each mode's system prompt and the tool description
s the model reads, manage skills per mode (saved versions, new skills, and imports from Codex, Claud
e Code, or a folder), create your own modes from templates, and merge built-in updates in one click
after a dsh upgrade.
## What it does
- **Understand each mode at a glance**: every mode gets a card that lists what it can do (run comman
ds, read and write files, browse the web, use subagents, and so on), so you can compare modes withou

t opening them.
- **Switch capabilities, not plugins**: 15 capabilities, one switch each. For exampl

e, turn off "Run commands" or make files read-only, without facing dozens of plugin names.
- **Edit
the prompt**: edit each mode's system prompt with a preview and a version history. You can also let
a saved prompt reach sessions that are already running, or let the model change the prompt in chat;

every save asks you first.
- **Edit tool descriptions**: rewrite the description of any tool the mod
el sees, for several modes at once, and restore the built-in text of one tool, one mode, or everythi

ng with one click. The tools' own definitions are never changed.
- **Create your own modes**: start

from four templates (Develop, Write, Chat, Read-only research), or copy any existing mode.
- **Contr
ol skills per mode**: turn a skill on or off in each mode or in all of them, pin a mode to a saved v
ersion of a skill, and keep a history of versions you can view, restore, or delete. Switching and pi

nning never move skill files.
- **Create and import skills**: write a new skill in the page, or copy
skills in from Codex, Claude Code, or any folder, several at once. When an imported skill's source

changes, the page says so and imports it again in one click.
- **Update the plugin itself**: the pag
e tells you when a newer version of this plugin exists and can install it with DSH's own installer,

after you confirm.
- **Keep up with dsh upgrades**: when dsh updates its built-in modes, merge the c
hanges in one click and keep yours. When a plugin fails to load, turn off just the failing plugins i

n one click.
- **When the page fails**: if the page itself fails to draw, it shows the error and **R
eload** instead of an empty section.
## Install
You need the dsh Web interface (`dsh web`). See Compatibility for supported versions.

## Features
### Capabilities
| Group | Capabilities |
| What it can do | Run commands, Files (with a separate **Allow file changes** switch), Web, Subagen

ts and workflows, Extend itself (plugin management, plugin market, plugin API lookup) |
| How it wor

ks | Plan mode, To-do list, Session goals, Skills, Ask you, Deliverables, Reminders |
| Context | Wo
rkspace instructions (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and similar), Time awareness, Context compaction |
- **Turning a capability on** restores it as the built-in mode has it. Plugins that switch by enviro
nment (such as Bash and PowerShell) go back to **Auto**, and plugins the built-in mode keeps off (su

ch as the Codex subagent) stay off.
- **Turning a capability off** switches off every plugin it incl

udes.
- A capability with only some of its plugins on is marked **Partly on**.
- Capabilities the mo
de has no plugins for are hidden; for example, dsh before 0.2.1 has no Reminders.
## Compatibility
| dsh version | Result |
| `0.2.0-rc.2` (npm `latest`) | Works. This dsh version provides no localized plugin names, so the p

lugin shows each plugin's official name instead |
| `0.2.1-alpha.3` | Works |
| `0.2.1-rc.1` (npm `n
ext`) | Works. rc.1 adds a plugin market tool to the built-in modes; modes you changed show "The bui
lt-in mode was updated", and syncing adds it switched off |
Every version above was installed and tested, including checks of the actual requests sent to the mo
del through a local mock model. The dsh APIs this plugin uses are not stable yet, so other versions
al mock model. The dsh APIs this plugin uses are not stable yet, so other versions may need changes.
## Known limitations
- **Sync needs a baseline**: syncing compares against the built-in plugin list recorded at your last
save. Modes changed with a version before 0.5.0 have no such record, so the first sync keeps every

difference from the built-in version as your change. Every save after that records a baseline.
- **S
cope of Live prompt**: it applies only to the opening and closing prompt text. The "complete prompt"

and "runtime context" settings still apply to new sessions only.
- **Scope of chat edits**: `mode_p

rompt` reads and writes only the opening prompt text.
- **Skills listed**: the page lists the skills
the modes find without a workspace: user, custom, and packaged skills. Project skills (`<project>/.

dsh/skills`, `<project>/.agents/skills`) depend on a session's workspace and are not listed.
- **Ski
lls written for other tools**: DSH reads `name`, `description`, `whenToUse`, `metadata`, `disable-mo
del-invocation`, and `user-invocable`; other fields, such as Claude Code's `allowed-tools` or `model
`, have no effect. A skill that relies on another tool's own tools (for example Codex's image genera

tion) is imported but may not work in DSH.
- **Where import looks**: `$CODEX_HOME/skills` (default `
~/.codex/skills`), `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/skills` (default `~/.claude/skills`), and `skills/<name>/SKIL
L.md` up to six levels below `~/.claude/plugins`, keeping the most recently changed copy of a plugin
cached in several versions. Project skills such as `<project>/.claude/skills` are imported through

**Folder**. A skill as a single `<name>.md` file is not listed.
- **Replacing on Windows**: the file
s are overwritten one by one, so a failure part way leaves a mix of old and new files. Restore the v

ersion saved before the import from the skill's version list.
- **A new skill just written**: the pa
ge waits 0.8 seconds for DSH's file watcher before it reads the list again. If a new skill still sho

ws "This mode cannot find it", click **Refresh**.
- **Skills turned off in every mode**: this needs

the policy row in every mode, so every built-in mode gets a profile override.
